raw_segments.text: So mayest thou live, till like ripe fruit thou drop into thy mother's lap, or be with
ease gathered nor harshly plucked, for death mature.
This is old age, but then thou must outlive thy youth, thy strength, thy beauty, which
will change to withered, weak, and grey.
Thy senses then obtuse, all taste of pleasure must forgo to what thou hast.
And for the air of youth, hopeful and cheerful, in thy blood will rain a melancholy damp of
cold, and dry to weigh thy spirits down, and last consume the balm of life, to whom
